resources.string: Enter your maximum heart rate to see training load, form and zones. Resting heart rate is measured while you sleep.
Breathing rate during sleep is clearly above usual, a common early sign of illness.

Readiness combines what your watch measured overnight with your recent training, each compared with your own normal, not with population averages.

HRV (35 %): the 7-day average of nightly HRV against your normal range from the last 60 days, as in HRV-guided training studies. Below the range means your body is still recovering; readiness then stays below "Ready to train" whatever else says.

Sleep (25 %): last night and the last three nights against your usual sleep, at least 7 and at most 9 hours.

Resting HR (20 %): last night's value against your usual. A raised resting heart rate often goes with fatigue or illness.

Training (20 %): form, fitness minus fatigue, against a band that grows with your fitness.

A breathing rate clearly above usual, together with low HRV or raised resting heart rate, holds readiness at 40 or below.

The weights are PacingLab's own choice and are not a validated score; the HRV comparison is the part with the strongest research behind it. Readiness needs 14 nights of HRV and settles after four to eight weeks.
